viewability.resolvedBy: Four user-uploaded local originals inspected on 2026-10-08
viewability.conceptSelected: Sunburst marker/camera hierarchy with restrained Nano Banana forest masses; generated geography rejected

params.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: preview-only art-direction study for Track Viewer 2.0 inside an original motorsport team-management game.
Primary request: a finished commercial-quality 2D tactical circuit viewer, Paddock Hybrid — Live Operations. Flat app screenshot, no physical device, no racing photograph. Deep ink/navy surfaces, calm layered ground materials, amber selected/actionable state, turquoise team identity. Refined mixed-case UI typography. The circuit and two managed cars are the focal points; scenery is quieter than track, and track quieter than selected-car identity. Strong legibility and restrained visual depth.

Style/medium: original simplified vector-like tactical site illustration with subtle 2.5D roofs and ground shadows; NOT photoreal satellite, NOT a toy city, NOT a 3D racing engine. Main track has a dark outer casing, subtly lighter asphalt, fine edges, a clear chequered start/finish and a distinct pit-lane/service area. No oversized thick track tubes or nearly invisible hairlines. Vehicle anchors sit ON their routes. Selected player car has a clear amber ring + readable abbreviation callout; second managed car a white shape/ring. Other cars are smaller, lower-priority team-colour dots, with selected/player labels first. Genuine tight clusters may overlap and are explained by a compact nearby-car list; never invent a stretched gap or displace car anchors.

Composition/framing: map dominates roughly 75 percent of the canvas, with a compact viewer header, unobtrusive camera tools near an edge, small selected-driver context strip and a narrow slice of existing driver strategy to suggest integration. Avoid rebuilding the entire command centre. Practical controls: Overview, Driver focus, Zoom in, Zoom out, Reset view, Expand, Environment on/off. All track + pit information still readable without scenery. No giant telemetry cards on the circuit. Spacious enough to remain meaningful in an enlarged laptop Track mode.

Supported context only: position, driver abbreviation, current tyre, existing status, gap/interval, nearby cars, pit state. No invented overtake probabilities, tyre life forecasts, pit predictions, wind, sector telemetry, radio, strategy AI, speedometers or charts. No proprietary game layout, official logo or trademark art. No neon, cyberpunk, holograms or colourful alarm banners. Natural environment is static and low contrast. Environmental placement here is a schematic art-direction study; never imply surveyed geography. Include a discreet footer "Stylized venue context". Clear hierarchy matters more than excessive scenery.

STUDY A — SUZUKA PREMIUM OVERVIEW. Recognizable real Suzuka figure-eight course: broad western Spoon loop, back-straight crossover, eastern Esses sequence, hairpin and final chicane. Preserve a single continuous racing course with one bridge crossover, not a literal symmetric number 8. North-up tactical plan, harmonious true proportions. Make the crossing understandable without inventing car elevation physics. Venue context comes from Suzuka's official venue map: simplified pit/paddock complex beside the main straight, main grandstand opposite the pits, Circuit Wheel in the amusement-park area beyond the main-grandstand side; restrained surrounding green areas. Buildings stay away from the racing line and pit car anchors. No arbitrary Ferris wheel in the infield or on the back straight. Render 22 cars with RUS selected and ANT second player; both same-team turquoise, selected RUS P6 Medium, ANT P8. Stable Overview mode. The viewer should feel like the flagship feature of a premium strategy game at 1920x1080, with a broad useful circuit canvas and clear tactical markers.

STUDY B — MONACO URBAN CIRCUIT. Recognizable irregular Monaco street-course outline with the uphill Casino section, tight hairpin, tunnel run and harbour-side chicane/Tabac/Piscine/Rascasse sequence. Low-contrast stylized Port Hercule and marina INSIDE the harbour-facing circuit section, water continuing toward the seaward side, simplified dense urban blocks landward/uphill. Refer conceptually to the Automobile Club de Monaco's official venue map, but do not reproduce its illustration. Do not put the marina at Casino or invent landmark geography. A few simplified marina piers/boats and terraces establish venue identity, not hundreds of tiny city shapes. Pit/paddock strip belongs alongside Boulevard Albert Ier between the start straight and Piscine section; no garage-by-garage claim. The circuit surface and car markers have stronger contrast than urban scenery. 22 cars, RUS selected P9 and ANT P11. Show Overview, quiet Environment on control, readable Reset/Expand. A premium original 2D site illustration, not satellite imagery or a copied racing-game map.

STUDY C — SPA PERMANENT FOREST CIRCUIT. Recognizable long triangular Spa-Francorchamps course with La Source hairpin, Eau Rouge/Raidillon, Kemmel/Les Combes, long sweeping southern loop and final Bus Stop. Surrounding natural context is a few subdued irregular forest masses and open motorsport clearings, not hundreds of toy trees. Original simplified pit building beside the start/finish straight, Raidillon grandstand at its actual track section, restrained paddock clearing. Use the official circuit access/site map as factual inspiration; do not copy it. Do not invent measured elevation, contour lines or elevation graphs. Flat tactical map with understated roof geometry and shallow ground shadows; no hills that obscure track. RUS selected P4 and ANT P5 close together, plus 20 competing cars; player labels remain readable, actual nearby anchors not moved apart artificially. Track stroke/lane is crisp against low-contrast forest. Medium environment detail. Distinct from Monaco and Suzuka while using the same Paddock Hybrid visual language.

STUDY D — TACTICAL DRIVER FOCUS. A zoomed section of Suzuka's main straight and pit approach, in the same viewer style as an Overview. Selected RUS P14 is on the main route, ANT P15 nearby on the same team. Four nearby competitors are genuinely close; small lower-priority dots remain anchored on the track and the selected driver's label has priority. An unobtrusive edge list identifies obscured nearby cars without spreading their positions. Distinct parallel pit lane with a competitor in service and another on exit, each placed on the route rather than on the racing straight. Quiet pit building supports lane context but does not cover markers. Driver focus mode is explicitly selected. Clear Overview and Reset view controls allow easy recovery, plus zoom +/- and Environment control. Small context strip says "RUS · P14 · Medium · Running"; no invented prediction or telemetry. Use a 4:3 map-focused composition suitable for an enlarged Track pane on laptop/tablet, not a cramped full desktop screenshot. Scenery intentionally sparse at focus zoom; camera smoothness is suggested by composition only, no speed trails or fictitious car movement.
